title: Orca Training — HealthKit export
description: One file per pull, written by the Claude iOS app into the Google Drive folder 'orca-health-exports'. Append-only: never edit a previous export. Omit any field that was not actually measured — never estimate or back-fill.

schemaVersion.description: Bump only on a breaking shape change.

pulledAt.description: When this pull ran, ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-08-22T07:30:00-07:00.

window.description: Inclusive date range this pull covers. Lets the consumer tell 'no runs in this window' apart from 'window not queried'.

notes.description: Free text from the pulling session — e.g. which data types were unavailable, or that the health integration needs reconnecting.

workouts.description: Every workout in the window, running and non-running alike. The consumer routes Running to SEEDED_ACTUALS and everything else to CROSS_TRAINING.

start.description: Local Seattle start time, HH:MM. Distinguishes two workouts on one date.

kind.description: HealthKit workout type: Running, Cycling, Ruck, Walking, Hiking, Strength, ...

mins.description: Elapsed duration in decimal minutes, e.g. 47.40 — matches the existing data.js convention.

hrAvg.description: Average heart rate, bpm. Omit if unavailable.

hrMax.description: Peak heart rate, bpm. Needs sample-level data — see the timezone gotcha in SKILL.md.

cadenceAvg.description: Average cadence in steps per minute (both feet).

source.description: Recording device, e.g. 'Apple Watch Series 9'. Useful when accuracy varies by source.

note.description: Anything notable — terrain, weather, pack weight, 'replaced Sat tempo'.

splits.description: Per-mile splits, in order. Powers decoupling and pacing-discipline analysis. Omit the whole array rather than inventing entries — a partial final mile is fine as a fractional 'mi'.

mi.description: Mile marker, 1-indexed. A trailing partial mile uses its fractional distance, e.g. 6.21.

hrAvg.description: Average bpm across this split — the key input for cardiac drift.

elevGainFt.description: Net elevation change across this split, feet. Negative for net downhill; contextualizes a slow or fast split.
